newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemeni team in London for talks on Eritrea dispute.
newsitem.headline: Yemeni team in London for talks on Eritrea dispute.

text.p: Senior Yemeni officials flew to London for the second stage of arbitration hearings to resolve a dispute with Eritrea over Red Sea islands near busy oil tanker routes, a Yemeni newspaper said on Monday.
The team, led by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Abdul-Karim al-Iryani, had travelled to London over the weekend and would begin work on Monday, the weekly Yemen Times said.

"This is the second stage of arbitration in which the two sides -- Yemen and Eritrea -- will file their responses to the initial positions of the other side," it said. "The two sides' rebuttals include documents, maps and other support evidence."
The five-judge arbitration panel, which first met in January, has the final say on the ownership of the disputed islands.

Yemen appointed an Egyptian and an American to the arbitration panel while Eritrea named an American and a Briton. Both countries agreed on a fifth member, British judge Sir Robert Jennings, to head the panel.
Arab Yemen and African Eritrea signed an accord in Paris last October to set up the arbitration court in London.
Both countries claim sovereignty over the small, arid Hanish islands. The dispute led to clashes in which at least 12 people died in December 1995.
